mainTopic: The date on a גט, when the three-month waiting period starts, when שמיטה cancels a כתובה, and documents written by day and signed at night.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about why חכמים required a date in every גט. A held-back גט is too rare to matter, because nobody rushes a divorce. A גט from overseas arrives late, but everyone knows that, so its date misleads no one. Next, רב and שמואל argue about when a divorced woman's three-month wait begins: from the giving or from the writing of the גט. Each side has a supporting ברייתא, and the הלכה follows שמואל: count from the writing. A second רב and שמואל dispute asks when שמיטה cancels a כתובה. רב requires both collecting part of it and setting it up as a loan, while שמואל says either step alone is enough. שמואל then rules that a כתובה, like a court document, may be written by day and signed at night. A story about רב's silence at his son's wedding turns out not to prove that he agrees. Finally, the גמרא explains why רבי שמעון allows a גט signed at night, and ריש לקיש limits that to a גט signed right away.

steps.title: A husband writes a גט but keeps it in his pocket
steps.stepSummary: The questioner asks about a husband who wrote and dated a גט but held onto it, hoping to make up with his wife, and gave it to her only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: What if he wrote the גט and put it in his pocket, thinking, 'If she makes peace with me, I'll make peace with her'? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question begun on the previous daf. It asks about a גט whose date is earlier than the day the wife actually receives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים required a date in a גט so everyone would know when the divorce took effect. In this case the date shows the day of writing, but the divorce only happens later when he hands it over. So the date is misleading, and the question is whether חכמים made any rule to deal with such a גט.

phrases.english: and he put it in his pocket —
phrases.notes: This finishes a question that began on the previous daf: the husband wrote the גט but held onto it.

phrases.english: thinking that if she appeases him, he will be appeased,
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous daf's discussion of why a גט must be dated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did חכמים make a rule for a גט that was written and dated but held back before being given?

steps.title: People do not prepare a divorce in advance
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that nobody rushes trouble onto himself, so this case is too rare for חכמים to make a rule about.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A person does not bring a calamity on himself ahead of time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. Normally a man does not write a גט until he is ready to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not claim this kind of גט is invalid. He says the case almost never happens, because writing a גט early means bringing trouble on yourself. חכמים made rules for common situations, so they did not need one here.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A person does not rush
a calamity upon himself.
phrases.notes: He means nobody prepares a divorce early, so this case is rare and the rabbis didn't need a rule for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is uncommon, because people do not write a גט before they really intend to divorce, so חכמים made no rule for it.

steps.title: Overseas גיטין arrive months after they are written
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי: a גט sent from overseas may be written in ניסן and arrive in תשרי, so its date is far off. What did the rule to date a גט accomplish?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Bills of divorce coming from overseas are written in ניסן and do not arrive until תשרי. What did חכמים accomplish with their enactment?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a new difficulty against the rule of dating a גט. This case cannot be called rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer worked because a held-back גט is uncommon. A גט sent from far away is common, and it always arrives long after the date written in it. So the dating rule seems to fail here, which is why the question works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: spring month / autumn month (about six months apart)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Bills of divorce that come from overseas,
which are written in Nisan
and do not arrive until Tishrei —
what did the Sages accomplish with their enactment?
phrases.notes: The enactment is the rule that every גט must have a date written in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rare case was answered, raises a common case that seems to defeat the dating rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The usefulness of the rabbinic rule requiring a date in a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An overseas גט is common and always arrives long after its date, so the date does not show when the divorce took effect.

steps.title: Everyone knows an overseas גט arrives late
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that overseas גיטין are publicly known to take effect later than their date, so nobody is misled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Those have publicity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule still works, because with an overseas גט everyone knows the date is only when it was written. Nobody will treat the divorce as starting on that date, so the woman would have to show when she actually received it. The dating rule stays in place for ordinary cases.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule of dating a גט is not undone by special cases. A held-back גט is too rare to matter, and an overseas גט is publicly known to arrive late.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Those have publicity.
phrases.notes: Literally 'they have a voice': everyone knows an overseas גט arrives late, so its date fools no one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the case: the late arrival is public knowledge, so the date misleads no one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An overseas גט seems to defeat the purpose of dating a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because everyone knows overseas גיטין arrive late, nobody relies on their date, and the dating rule still serves its purpose.

steps.title: When does the waiting period after a גט begin?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: from when do we count the three months a divorced woman waits before remarrying? רב says from when the גט is given. שמואל says from when it is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: From when do we count for a גט? רב says: from the time it is given. שמואל says: from the time it is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new מחלוקת with the word איתמר. The next steps challenge שמואל, bring a ברייתא for each side, and end with the final הלכה in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorced woman must wait three months before remarrying. For רב the count starts when the divorce actually takes effect, at the giving. For שמואל the count already starts at the writing, so a woman who received an old גט may have less time left to wait.
steps.confusionAlert: Both רב and שמואל agree the divorce itself takes effect only when the גט is given. They disagree only about when the three-month waiting count begins.

phrases.english: It was stated:
From when does one count for a bill of divorce?
phrases.notes: This is counting the three months a divorced woman waits before she may remarry.

phrases.english: Rav says: From the time of giving,
and Shmuel says: From the time of writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the dating of a גט to a new question about the waiting period.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the three months are counted from the giving of the גט. שמואל: they are counted from its writing.

steps.title: Two women in one courtyard with different rules
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר הושעיא challenges שמואל: people will see two women divorced on the same day, one forbidden to remarry and one permitted, and find it strange.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר הושעיא objected to שמואל: people will say, 'Two women in one courtyard, and this one is forbidden while that one is permitted!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's view that the three months are counted from when the גט was written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture two women who both get their גט on the same day. One גט was written that day and the other was written months earlier. Under שמואל, the second woman may remarry right away while the first must wait, and onlookers will find that strange.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it (he raised a challenge)
Courtyard (a shared living space where neighbors see each other's lives)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Hoshaya objected to Shmuel:
People will say: two women in one courtyard,
phrases.notes: He means two women who got their גיטין at the same time, but one גט was written much earlier than the other.

phrases.english: this one is forbidden and that one is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's position from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that the count starts from the writing of the גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two women divorced at the same moment would get different rules, which looks confusing and unfair to onlookers.

steps.title: The date on each גט explains the difference
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that each woman's גט carries its own date, so anyone can see why one may remarry and the other may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: For this one, the date of her גט proves her status, and for that one, the date of her גט proves her status.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends שמואל by pointing to the date written on each גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between the two women is not hidden. Each גט shows when it was written, so anyone who checks can see that one woman's three months have already passed and the other's have not.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
For this one, the date of her divorce document proves her status,
and for that one, the date of her divorce document proves her status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the apparent contradiction has a visible explanation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: People would be confused by two women divorced together having different rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each גט's date openly explains its owner's status, so nobody is misled.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is a ברייתא for each side, then quotes the one for רב: if a messenger takes three months on the road, the woman still waits three months after she gets the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא like רב and there is a ברייתא like שמואל. The one like רב: If a man sends a גט to his wife and the messenger is delayed on the way for three months, once the גט reaches her hand she must wait three months. We are not worried that it is an 'old גט', because he was not alone with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first announces that each side has a supporting ברייתא, setting up two proofs, and then brings the proof for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three months already passed since the writing, yet the ברייתא still makes her wait three months from when she received it. This shows that the count starts from the giving, just as רב says.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that matches his view
An 'old גט': one after which the husband was alone with his wife

steps.confusionAlert: The line about a גט ישן is not the proof. It only says the delayed גט is still valid, because he was not alone with her. The proof for רב is that she must still wait three full months after receiving it.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with Rav,
and it is taught in a baraita in line with Shmuel.
It is taught in line with Rav:
One who sends a divorce document to his wife,
and the messenger was delayed on the way three months,
when the document reaches her hand,
she must wait three months;
and we are not concerned about an 'old divorce document',
phrases.notes: An 'old גט' is one where the husband was alone with his wife after it was written, which would make it a problem.

phrases.english: since he was not alone with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the core מחלוקת of step 5 and brings a source for רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the count starts from the giving of the גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a messenger delayed three months, where she still waits three months after receiving the גט.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא for שמואל: if a man leaves a גט with a third person to give after three months, she may remarry right away once she gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא like שמואל: If a man deposits a גט for his wife with someone and says, 'Do not give it to her until after three months,' once he gives it to her she may remarry immediately. We are not worried that it is an 'old גט', because he was not alone with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second promised proof, this one supporting שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three months passed between the writing and the giving, and the ברייתא lets her remarry as soon as she receives it. So the waiting period was already counting from the writing, just as שמואל says.

keyTerms.meaning: One who deposits something with a third person

phrases.english: It is taught in line with Shmuel:
One who deposits a divorce document for his wife with a third person,
and said to him: Do not give it to her
until after three months,
once he gave it to her, she is permitted to marry immediately;
and we are not concerned about an 'old divorce document',
since he was not alone with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of the two promised proofs, parallel to step 8 but for the other side.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the count starts from the writing of the גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a גט held by a third person for three months, after which she may remarry immediately.

steps.title: How later אמוראים acted in practice
steps.stepSummary: Some אמוראים counted from the writing, others from the giving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא, רב פפי and רב אשי acted from the time of writing. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע acted from the time of giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that later אמוראים split in actual practice, setting up the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת did not stay theoretical. Each group of אמוראים ruled for real cases according to one side: the first group like שמואל, the second like רב.

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב פַּפֵּי וְרַב אָשֵׁי –
phrases.english: Rav Kahana, Rav Pappi and Rav Ashi
would act from the time of writing,

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ –
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
would act from the time of giving.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב פַּפֵּי וְרַב אָשֵׁי עָבְדִי מִשְּׁעַת כְּתִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proofs for both sides, reports how the dispute played out in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Later אמוראים were split in practice between counting from the writing and counting from the giving.

steps.title: The הלכה: count from the writing
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling is that the three months are counted from when the גט was written, like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: from the time of writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the מחלוקת and rules like שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though each side had a supporting ברייתא and practice was split, the final הלכה follows שמואל. The three-month wait starts from the date written on the גט, not from when she received it.
steps.whatToRemember: A divorced woman's three-month wait is counted from when the גט was written (שמואל), not from when it was handed to her (רב).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for when a divorced woman may remarry.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: from the time of writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two practices reported in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows שמואל: the three months are counted from the writing of the גט.

steps.title: When does a כתובה get canceled by שמיטה
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute: רב says a כתובה is canceled by שמיטה only once the woman both collected part and set it up as a loan. שמואל says either one alone is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: From when is a כתובה canceled by שמיטה? רב says: once she collects part of it and sets the rest up as a loan. שמואל says: if she collected part, even without setting it up as a loan, or if she set it up as a loan, even without collecting part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new argument between רב and שמואל: at what point a כתובה becomes a normal debt that שמיטה wipes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular loans are canceled by שמיטה, but a כתובה starts out as a special promise rather than a loan. רב requires two steps (collecting part and setting it up as a loan) before it counts as a loan. שמואל says either step alone turns it into a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract; the husband's promised payment to his wife
Formally setting up the amount as a loan in בית דין

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a new רב and שמואל dispute about documents, and it follows the same pattern as the one just finished: two opinions, then a ברייתא for each side.

phrases.english: It was stated:
From when is a marriage contract canceled [by the Sabbatical Year]?
Rav says:
From when she collects part and establishes [the rest as a loan].
And Shmuel says:

phrases.aramaic: פָּגְמָה – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא זָקְפָה,
phrases.english: If she collected part, even though she did not establish it [as a loan],

phrases.aramaic: זָקְפָה – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא פָּגְמָה.
phrases.english: or if she established it [as a loan], even though she did not collect part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new רב and שמואל dispute after the date-of-the-גט discussion was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: שמיטה cancels a כתובה only after both פגימה and זקיפה. שמואל: either פגימה or זקיפה alone is enough.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is a ברייתא for each side, then quotes the one for רב: a כתובה is canceled only after she both collects part and sets it up as a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא like רב and a ברייתא like שמואל. The one like רב: From when is a כתובה canceled? Once she collects part and sets it up as a loan. If she collected part but did not set it up, or set it up but did not collect part, it is not canceled until she does both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says each side has a supporting ברייתא, and first quotes the one that matches רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא matches רב word for word: both steps are needed. It also rejects שמואל's view, because it says one step alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with his view
Until: here, not until both steps happen

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav,
and it is taught in a baraita in accordance with Shmuel.
It is taught in accordance with Rav:
From when is a marriage contract canceled?
From when she collects part and establishes [it as a loan].
If she collected part but did not establish it,
or established it but did not collect part,
it is not canceled,
until she collects part and establishes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting רב's opinion from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that both פגימה and זקיפה are needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states explicitly that one step alone does not make the כתובה cancelable

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא for שמואל: payments like אונס, קנס, פיתוי and a כתובה are canceled by שמיטה once they are set up as a loan, and that happens when the case stands in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא like שמואל: payments for rape, a fine, seduction, and a woman's כתובה, if they were set up as a loan, are canceled by שמיטה. If not, they are not canceled. From when are they set up as a loan? From the time they stand in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the ברייתא that supports שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a כתובה is canceled once it was set up as a loan, and says nothing about collecting part. This shows that זקיפה alone is enough, as שמואל said. It also tells us when זקיפה happens: when the case stands before בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment owed by a man who raped a girl
Payment owed by a man who seduced a girl
Standing in court, when בית דין rules on the case

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a כתובה is canceled by שמיטה only after both פגימה and זקיפה. שמואל: either one is enough. Each has a supporting ברייתא, and זקיפה happens when the case stands in בית דין.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא never mentions collecting part. That silence is the point: setting it up as a loan alone is enough, which is שמואל's view.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Shmuel:
[Payment for] rape, a fine, and seduction,
and a woman's marriage contract,
that were established as a loan, are canceled [by the Sabbatical Year];
and if not, they are not canceled.
From when are they established as a loan?
From the time of standing in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second promised ברייתא, which supports שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that זקיפה alone is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא making cancellation depend only on being set up as a loan, which happens at the court hearing

steps.title: A כתובה may be written by day and signed at night
steps.stepSummary: שמואל compares a כתובה to a court document. Court documents may be written by day and signed at night, so a כתובה may be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A כתובה is like a court document. Court documents may be written by day and signed at night, so a כתובה may also be written by day and signed at night.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new rule: a כתובה does not have to be written and signed on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a גט written by day and signed at night is a problem. שמואל says a כתובה belongs in a different group, the group of court documents, where this gap is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage document listing what the husband owes his wife
A court document or court action
Written during the day and signed at night

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A כתובה is like a court document.
Just as court documents
may be written by day and signed at night,
so too a כתובה may be written by day
and signed at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּתוּבָּה כְּמַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about כתובה: writing by day and signing at night
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתובה is treated like a court document, so it may be written by day and signed at night.

steps.title: רב stayed silent at his son's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The כתובה of רבי חייא בר רב was written by day and signed at night. רב was there and said nothing, which suggests he agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כתובה of רבי חייא בר רב was written by day and signed at night. רב was there and did not say anything to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that seems to show רב agrees with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If writing by day and signing at night made a כתובה invalid, רב would have objected. His silence looks like approval, and that is the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not say anything at all to them

phrases.english: The כתובה of Rabbi Chiya bar Rav
was written by day and signed at night;
Rav was there
and he did not say anything to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתוּבְּתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר רַב אִיכְּתוּב בַּיּוֹם וְאִיחֲתוּם בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to support שמואל's rule
steps.raayaObject: That רב also allows a כתובה written by day and signed at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's silence when his son's כתובה was signed at night

steps.title: Does רב agree with שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the story proves that רב holds like שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב holds like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the story really proves that רב agrees with שמואל. This sets up the next step, which will question the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לימא (shall we say) usually signals that the גמרא is about to reject the suggested conclusion. So the learner should expect a push-back.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It often opens an idea the גמרא will reject
He holds, meaning this is his opinion

phrases.english: Shall we say he holds like Shmuel?
phrases.notes: "He" is רב, who was silent in the story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the story seems to prove
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב's silence shows that he agrees with שמואל

steps.title: They were busy with the כתובה the whole time
steps.stepSummary: No proof: the scribe and witnesses kept working on that כתובה from day into night, so it is a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were busy with that same matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The people writing and signing kept working on the כתובה without stopping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people stayed with the document the whole time, the gap between day and night does not count as a real break. So רב's silence only shows that this kind of case is fine. It does not show that he agrees with שמואל in general.

keyTerms.meaning: Busy with that same matter, without stopping

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say רב disagrees with שמואל. It only says this story cannot prove that he agrees.

phrases.english: They were busy with that same matter.
phrases.notes: He means the scribe and witnesses kept working on the כתובה from day until it was signed at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רב's silence
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the story is rejected, not שמואל's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was a special case where everyone stayed busy with the כתובה, which is valid anyway

steps.title: A ברייתא: continuous work makes it valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק teaches that writing by day and signing at night is invalid only when the people were not busy with it the whole time. If they were, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק said: They taught this only when the people were not busy with that matter. But if they were busy with that matter, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its rejection with a ברייתא showing that continuous work makes the document valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that a document written by day and signed at night is invalid has a limit. When the people never stopped working on it, it is valid. That covers the case of רב's son, so the story proves nothing about שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case where

steps.whatToRemember: The story about רב cannot prove he agrees with שמואל. The case was valid anyway, because the people stayed busy with the כתובה the whole time.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Tzadok said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ, אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁאֵין עֲסוּקִין בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן,
phrases.english: They taught this only when they were not busy with that matter,
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule that a document written by day and signed at night is invalid.

phrases.english: but if they were busy with that matter, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי צָדוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the rejection in the previous step
steps.raayaObject: That a document is valid when the people stayed busy with it from day into night
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בר רבי צדוק

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון allow it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבי שמעון allows a גט written by day and signed at night. רבא asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי שמעון says it is valid. רבא said: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for the reason behind רבי שמעון's lenient view. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים in the משנה call such a גט invalid. רבא wants to know why רבי שמעון is not worried about the gap between writing and signing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says it is valid:
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה, about a גט written by day and signed at night.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is Rabbi Shimon's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כתובה discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי שמעון allows a גט written by day and signed at night

steps.title: Once he decides to divorce, he loses the produce
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: רבי שמעון holds that once the husband decides to divorce his wife, he no longer has the right to the produce of her property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: once the husband has set his mind on divorcing her, he no longer has the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains רבי שמעון's reason: the husband loses his rights to the produce as soon as he decides to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing the גט shows the husband has already decided to divorce. So the date of writing is a fair date for when his rights to the produce end, even if the signing came later.

keyTerms.meaning: Set his eyes on divorcing her, meaning he decided to divorce her
Produce, the income from the wife's property that the husband normally gets

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the date on a גט to money: the date decides when the husband's right to the produce ends.

phrases.english: He holds: once he has set his eyes on divorcing her,
he no longer has the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנָּתַן עֵינָיו לְגָרְשָׁהּ, שׁוּב אֵין לוֹ פֵּירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband loses the produce once he decides to divorce, so the gap between writing and signing does not matter

steps.title: ריש לקיש: only if it is signed right away
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits רבי שמעון's view: the גט is valid only if it was signed right away, not if the signing came days later.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי שמעון said it is valid only if it was signed right away. But if the signing was delayed from now until ten days later, it is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש narrows רבי שמעון's leniency to a גט signed soon after it was written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Signing the same night is fine for רבי שמעון. A long delay, such as ten days, is not covered by his leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: From now until ten days later, meaning a long delay

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֶלָּא לְאַלְתַּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said it is valid only if it was signed right away,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִכָּאן וְעַד עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים – לֹא;
phrases.english: but if the delay was from now until ten days later, it is not valid;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לֹא הִכְשִׁיר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אֶלָּא לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on רבי שמעון's lenient view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון allows a גט signed only shortly after writing, not one signed after a long delay.
